sections.history: Chatravata Narasimha, also written Kshatravata, stands a short distance south of Lower Ahobilam, within easy reach of the village and on the same route as Yogananda Narasimha. It is one of the nine Narasimha shrines of the Ahobilam pilgrimage. Its name is usually explained by the tree beneath which the Lord was found, its spreading crown an umbrella, or chatra, over the image. The shrine is part of the worship of the nine forms maintained by the Ahobila Matha, and its building is generally associated with the Vijayanagara centuries, when Ahobilam's temples were generously endowed.
sections.architecture: The temple is small and set among trees and fields, with an enclosure wall and a simple pillared hall before the sanctum. The image is what draws devotees: Narasimha sits at ease with a gentle smile, and his left hand is held in the tala mudra, the gesture of keeping rhythm — a pose seldom seen in images of Narasimha anywhere else.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that two gandharvas, the celestial singers Haha and Huhu, came to this place and sang before the Lord, and that Narasimha, delighted, kept time to their music with his hand and blessed them to excel among singers in all the three worlds. For this reason the shrine is cherished by musicians and by those who seek skill in the arts. In the astrological reading of the nine shrines, Chatravata is linked with Ketu.
sections.festivals: Narasimha Jayanti and the annual Brahmotsavam of Ahobilam are the main occasions, when the shrines near Lower Ahobilam see a steady flow of pilgrims. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: One of the easiest of the nine to visit, Chatravata is close to Lower Ahobilam and reached by road. After the severity of the hill shrines it is a cheerful place — look for the hand keeping time. Pair it with Yogananda Narasimha on the same short outing.

visit.timings: Worship is offered daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday closure. Confirm current timings locally.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Lower Ahobilam is reached by road via Allagadda; Nandyal is the nearest major railhead. Chatravata Narasimha is a short drive south of Lower Ahobilam, on the route to Yogananda Narasimha; local autos and jeeps are available.
